assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new class of electronic matter with a topological invariant and protected boundary states, predicted in theory and then realised in real materials (HgTe quantum wells, Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 surfaces). Original, clearly delineated and broadly reshaping condensed matter physics, materials discovery and device concepts. From a materials-physics view it is a case where theory and well-controlled interface/crystal growth and spectroscopy converge.
assessment.attribution: The decisive chain is theory of the quantum spin Hall state (Kane with Mele), the first experimental demonstration in HgTe (Molenkamp's group), and the first 3D topological insulator spectroscopy (Hasan). Three names can carry this, but Mele and the HgTe-proposal theorists are not all accommodated, so the allocation is a genuine judgement. I would favour Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, from my recollection of the field rather than independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Close to two decades of independent confirmation across many groups and materials; the interpretation is stable and the field is widely applied. Timely, and arguably a long-standing omission.
uncertainties: Credit split between Kane and Mele and the other early theorists is contested and cannot be settled from the supplied text.
Which experimental 3D topological-insulator work is decisive (several groups reported near-simultaneously) is unresolved.
Overlap with the separate ballot entry that includes quantum anomalous Hall; I rank only this one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice concept and its realisation, followed by Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability, opened a new regime of precision measurement. A clear invention with immediate consequences for timekeeping, tests of fundamental physics and geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and made the first Sr clocks; Ye brought the clocks to systematic uncertainty at the 10^-18 level. Two names give a tidy and fair configuration; others (e.g. Lemke, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom) are not on the credited list. Pairing is based on my recollection.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs and species confirm the performance; the work is well developed and mature. Redefinition of the SI second is still pending, but that is an application milestone, not a scientific doubt.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Ye versus other contributors (e.g. Hall's earlier frequency comb work already recognised in 2005) is somewhat subjective.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the SI second redefinition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle followed by experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the whole field of moire materials. Highly original, conceptually clean and with strong experimental follow-up. As a microscopist I value that the structure is directly tunable and imageable.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is the clear theory origin; the 2018 experiments from Jarillo-Herrero's group are the decisive demonstration. Three names fit naturally, and the credited set contains no extraneous names, which is helpful.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely within a few years and extended to many moire systems, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated phases is not fully settled. Somewhat young relative to other candidates, yet the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Possible concern that the field is still evolving and credit to Cao and other experimental authors is not representable within three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal gave a concrete architecture for quantum computation with trapped ions, and Blatt's group and others demonstrated gates, algorithms and error-corrected operations. A coherent theory-to-experiment story with major influence on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller for the proposal; Blatt for experimental realisation of the gate and subsequent scaling. Wineland's earlier recognition in 2012 and the roles of Monroe and others in the ion-trap programme make allocation delicate, but the three credited names are defensible.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across many groups and platforms; trapped ions remain a leading platform. Mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) and the other Cirac-Zoller candidate entries on the longlist.
Weight between the Innsbruck group and the NIST/Maryland ion-trap programme is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED combined theory (Blais et al.) and experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf) to achieve strong coupling of microwave photons to superconducting qubits, the basis for dispersive readout and for modern superconducting quantum processors. Important, original, and clearly an invention that enabled a platform.
assessment.attribution: Proposal and theory by Blais, with Schoelkopf and Wallraff as experimental leaders; the three-name configuration is reasonable. The relation to recent recognition of superconducting-circuit quantum effects is a consideration I cannot fully assess from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with many independent groups and an industry-scale follow-on. The question is whether it is distinct enough from previously honoured superconducting circuit work.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with earlier recognition of macroscopic quantum phenomena in superconducting circuits; I treat this as an unverified consideration.
Role of Devoret, Nakamura and others in the broader field is outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and an identified source (the blazar TXS 0506+056, plus the Galactic plane) opened neutrino astronomy at energies far above earlier solar and supernova neutrinos. A discovery in the sense of the prize criteria, requiring a decades-long instrument effort.
assessment.attribution: The idea and leadership of the IceCube detector are associated with Halzen; Karle is a key figure in construction and analysis. A large collaboration weakens a clean attribution, and others in the project's history (and other pioneers of the field) are not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established; individual source identification is more recent and still being refined. Confirmation by other detectors is limited so far.
uncertainties: Whether the individual-source evidence is yet strong enough.
Large-collaboration attribution and the absence of other pioneers from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nd-Fe-B is the strongest known commercial permanent magnet and underlies motors, generators, drives and storage devices. It is a clear invention, which fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion, and a materials-physics success where microstructure (grain boundaries, Nd-rich phases) controls performance.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered) and Croat (melt-spun) made independent near-simultaneous discoveries in 1983-84; two names is a natural fit, though independence and priority is a recognised subtlety.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and well-understood; fully mature and arguably overdue if the committee accepts materials inventions as physics.
uncertainties: Whether the work is regarded as physics rather than materials engineering.
Priority and the role of other contributors such as Herbst are not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnelling magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions (1995), then very large effects with crystalline MgO barriers, enabled hard-disk read heads and MRAM. The interfacial structure and epitaxy of oxide barriers is central, which I find compelling from an electron-microscopy perspective. An invention with strong technology reach.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, with Yuasa and others (and Parkin) delivering MgO-based giant TMR. Three names is plausible, but Parkin and Butler/Mathon theory are not in the credited set, so the fairness of allocation is questionable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with commercial deployment; recognition is timely but spintronics was already honoured in 2007 (GMR).
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize for GMR and unrepresented key contributors such as Parkin.
Whether the committee sees it as a sufficiently distinct discovery.
